title: Book One · Chapter 50: The Heavy Bag
story:
Mrs Lan comes through the gate with two bags. One holds vegetables. The other holds a small sack of rice.

Ronan runs to take the rice bag. She lifts it away. His hands close on air.

“Not that one.”

“I can carry things.”

“I know. This little bag is very heavy.”

He feels upset. He helped with the moving cart. He helped clean the floor, too. Why will she not let him carry this bag?

Mrs Lan takes three more steps. The vegetable bag slips from her other arm. Ronan grabs it. A cabbage rolls against the side and pushes one tomato out of the open top.

The tomato hits the stone and breaks.

Everyone looks at it. The black cat comes closer, then decides against it.

“I was helping,” Ronan says.

Mrs Lan sets both bags down. “You were trying. I needed a question first. Ask me about the right handle.”

Mum comes from the kitchen. She brings a bowl for the split tomato and a cloth for the stone. The good part can go into soup. The dirty part goes away.

Ronan waits for Mrs Lan to ask him to pay for the tomato. Mrs Lan doesn't say that. She gives him the light bunch of greens. He can carry those in his arms. She will carry the rice herself.

“Where do you want these greens?” he asks. She points to the front kitchen shelf. He puts them there. He leaves the other bags alone.

After lunch, he tells Leo the story. “Mrs Lan could ask for help first,” Leo says. “Then she would not drop things.”

“She didn't drop the tomato,” Ronan says. “I pulled the bag.”

Leo makes a little falling shape with one hand. Then he stops. Ronan isn't laughing yet.

They take the map out to check the road to Mr Qiu's stall. Mum needs a spool of black thread. She comes with them. On the way, they see a woman with a basket. She is trying to hold a door open. The basket makes that hard.

Ronan begins to move toward the basket, then asks, “Can I hold the door for you?”

“Yes, please. Stand on that side. Keep your fingers clear of the edge.”

She points to a place. He holds the door from there. Leo waits clear of the step. The woman gets through and thanks them. Nothing falls. It is a quick job. Ronan did not lift anything heavy.

At the stall, Mr Qiu is sorting books. Leo offers to put a pile on a higher shelf.

“No thanks,” Mr Qiu says. “Those go home tonight. Please hold this cloth. The wind will blow it away.”

Leo puts one hand on the cloth. It seems a very small job. Leo keeps his hand there. Ronan buys the thread for Mum.

They reach the green gate. Mrs Lan finished her soup a little earlier. She gives Mum a little bowl with tomato pieces in it. A little tomato skin curls up at one edge. Ronan remembers that broken piece. Mrs Lan used the good part in her soup.

“Recovered,” Mrs Lan says.

“Not all of it,” Ronan answers.

“No. Enough for soup.”

“Where do these bags go?” he asks. Mrs Lan points to her front room. He takes them there. Then he sits on the step and draws a cabbage on a spare paper corner.

The cabbage is round and serious. Leo adds two tiny legs underneath, so it can carry itself next time. Ronan laughs at last. Mrs Lan looks at the legs on their cabbage. “I would buy one like that,” she says. “It could walk home by itself.”
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：heavy＝重的；handle＝提手；soup＝汤；No thanks＝不用，谢谢。

理解问题：

1. Ronan 的帮助为什么一开始反而添了麻烦？
2. 他后来怎样先问清楚需要？
